Hi Samir —

Thanks — answering your questions and attaching a short code-first note. High level: Redwood supports three recommended patterns depending on threat model and UX: 

A) Server-to-server (recommended for batch scoring / backend integrations)
- Use a Redwood service account credential (managed in Console or via KMS/HSM-backed key).
- Service account issues JWTs signed with the account's private key; Redwood validates JWT on incoming requests.
- Rotation: programmatic rotation is supported via our Management API (POST /v1/service-accounts/{id}/keys) — you can create/deprecate keys and set a primary key. We also surface key metadata in the Console and expose audit logs.

B) Backend-minted short-lived tokens (recommended for client UX)
- Your backend exchanges the service account credential for a short-lived token (exp 1–15m) via Redwood's token minting endpoint.
- Short-lived tokens scoped by route and model; they are safe to use in the browser because they are ephemeral and auditable.

C) API keys (legacy / machine-to-machine)
- Long-lived API keys are supported but we recommend scoping and rotating them frequently.

Sample SDK snippets (Node, pseudo):
- createServiceKey() -> Management API to create key and return id
- mintShortToken(serviceKeyId, scope, ttl) -> returns ephemeral_token
- callInference(ephemeral_token, payload) -> inference result

Audit & logs: we emit per-request logs with key_id, service_account_id, subject_claim, model_used, and latency. Logs are queryable via our Console and streaming webhook.

Next steps: I'll attach a one-page playbook and a minimal Node example in the follow-up. Happy to review your rotation cadence in the meeting — if you have a preferred rotation window we can validate feasibility.

Cheers,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
